faq: Does it work with older vintage themes?
App embeds work on any theme. App blocks need Online Store 2.0 themes with sections everywhere. For vintage themes we suggest an embed with a clear setup step.
Can the block show live data from my app?
Yes. We fetch data through an app proxy or store it in metafields, whichever suits your case. Both keep the storefront fast and avoid exposing keys in the browser.
Will it slow down the storefront?
We keep the scripts small, load them only where the block appears and defer anything heavy. The Premium package includes a speed check so you can see the effect.
Yes. Removing the block or turning off the embed leaves no code behind in the theme files, which is one of the main reasons to use theme app extensions.
desc:
Shopify theme app extensions and blocks let merchants add your app to their storefront without editing theme code. Ecom Swift LLC builds app blocks and app embeds with theme editor settings, live data from your app and short setup instructions for merchants.

## What are Shopify theme app extensions?

A theme app extension is the part of a Shopify app that appears on the storefront. It comes in two forms. An app block is a component a merchant adds to a section in the theme editor, such as a review widget on a product page. An app embed loads across the whole store, such as a chat button or a tracking script. Merchants turn them on, move them and adjust their settings in the theme editor, with no code.

## Why the old way of adding app code causes trouble

Before app blocks, apps often asked merchants to paste snippets into theme files or injected scripts into the page. That left code behind after uninstall, broke when the theme was updated and made support harder. Merchants avoided the apps, or hired developers to install them.

Theme app extensions solve this. Everything is declared in the app, the merchant controls placement, and removing the app removes its blocks. That makes installation easier for the merchant and cleaner for you.

## How good storefront blocks affect your app

For a storefront app, the block is the product. If it is hard to place, looks wrong in the merchant's theme or slows the page, merchants judge the whole app by it. A block that adapts to the theme's fonts and colors looks like part of the store and gets used.

Speed counts as well. Visitors do not know which app made a page slow, but merchants find out, and they remove the app. Light code that loads only when needed protects both your install base and the store's shoppers.

## What a good theme app extension includes

- App blocks that merchants add from the theme editor.
- App embeds for features needed across the store.
- Theme editor settings, such as text, colors, layout and toggles.
- Support for Online Store 2.0 themes and their section structure.
- Live data from your app through an app proxy or metafields.
- Styles that inherit theme fonts and spacing.
- Lazy loading and a check of the effect on page speed.
- A link in your admin that opens the theme editor at the right place.
- A short illustrated setup guide for merchants.

## How we build it

We start from what the block should show and where merchants will want it. We build it as a theme app extension in your app, using Liquid, CSS and light JavaScript, and connect it to your data. We then test it on several themes, including Dawn, because themes handle spacing and fonts differently.

The Basic package delivers one app block with a few editor settings. Standard adds a second block, an app embed, live data and testing on three themes. Premium delivers a full set of blocks and embeds with the admin shortcut, speed checks, a setup guide and testing on five themes. We cannot test every theme in existence, so we recommend a list of supported themes.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Keep settings few and labeled in plain words.
- Use theme fonts and colors by default.
- Provide clear instructions with screenshots for merchants.
- Test with several themes, not only your own.

**Avoid:**
- Asking merchants to paste code into theme files.
- Loading large scripts on every page.
- Hard-coded colors that clash with the store.
- Leaving data behind when the block is removed.

## Who this service is for

App developers who need a storefront component but are more comfortable with backend work. Teams whose app still uses script tags or manual snippets. Owners who get support requests about installation and want setup to be simple.

## What we need from you

Repository access, collaborator access to your Partner Dashboard, a development store and a description of what the block should show. Tell us which themes your merchants use most. We never ask for passwords.
